findings.evidence: SmoothParameter.lean References list only the roadmap; picardResidual + hasStrictFDerivAt_picardResidual_path (identity path-derivative) + hR.implicitFunction is exactly the Lang/Abraham–Marsden proof strategy. mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/ODE/PicardLindelof.lean:675 and ExistUnique.lean provide only existence/uniqueness, not smooth parameter dependence.
findings.fix: Add the textbook source of the implicit-function-theorem-on-the-Picard-operator argument to the References (e.g. Lang or Abraham–Marsden), the same way InvariantVectorField.lean and IntegralCurve.lean name their adapted sources.
findings.issue: The file's proof plan — write the Picard integral equation as a zero of a map between Banach spaces of continuous paths (picardResidual), show its path-derivative at the base solution is the identity, and invoke the Banach implicit function theorem to get smooth dependence on the parameter — is the standard functional-analytic proof of smoothness of ODE flows (Lang, Differential and Riemannian Manifolds, Ch. IV; Abraham–Marsden–Ratiu). Mathlib has only Picard–Lindelöf existence, not this result, so it is not a Mathlib adaptation, but the informal source of the proof is unnamed; the References section cites only the roadmap.

summary: The Mathlib-adapted lemmas (invariant vector field, integral-curve chart calculation) are properly credited. The core smooth-parameter-dependence construction follows the classical Banach implicit-function-theorem proof of ODE flow smoothness but names no mathematical source, citing only the roadmap.
